# Finiteness of groups generated by asynchronous transducers is undecidable

No algorithm decides whether a given asynchronous transducer is periodic. Consequently the finiteness problem for groups generated by invertible asynchronous transducers is unsolvable.

An asynchronous transducer is a tuple $(\Sigma, Q, q_0, \lambda)$ with a finite alphabet $\Sigma$, a finite set of states $Q$, an initial state $q_0 \in Q$ and a transition function $\lambda\colon Q \times \Sigma \to Q \times \Sigma^*$. On an infinite input $a_1a_2a_3\cdots \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ it produces states and output words by $(q_i, \beta_i) = \lambda(q_{i-1}, a_i)$ and outputs $\beta_1\beta_2\cdots$. It is nondegenerate if every infinite input gives an infinite output; it then determines the rational function $f\colon \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}} \to \Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ sending an input to its output. It is invertible if $f$ is a homeomorphism, and periodic if some iterate $f^m$ with $m \ge 1$ is the identity.

1. There is no algorithm that decides, given an asynchronous transducer, whether it is periodic (Theorem 1.2 of the source).
2. There is no algorithm that decides, given a finite collection of invertible asynchronous transducers, whether the group generated by their rational homeomorphisms is finite (Theorem 1.3 of the source).

The finiteness problem for groups generated by synchronous automata, which output exactly one letter per letter read, is not settled by this result.

## Expansion

The rational group $\mathcal{R}$ of Grigorchuk, Nekrashevych and Sushchanskii is the group of rational homeomorphisms of $\Sigma^{\mathbb{N}}$ defined by invertible transducers. The source shows that $\mathcal{R}$ contains a subgroup isomorphic to $2V$, effectively: every element of $2V$ is topologically conjugate to a rational function given by a transducer computed from it. A periodic transducer is one of finite order in $\mathcal{R}$, so deciding periodicity would solve the torsion problem of $2V$. The cyclic group generated by a single invertible transducer is finite exactly when the transducer is periodic, so the finiteness problem is unsolvable already for one generator.
